ds_context: The water-cooled condenser is a critical component of power generation systems, and its failure can lead to significant downtime and increased maintenance costs. The main failure modes of the condenser include leakage and erosion of condenser tubes, failure of condenser fan bearings, and leakage in the condenser shell, cooling water pumps, and circulating water system. These failures can be attributed to poor quality of components, inadequate maintenance, high temperature and pressure, aggressive cooling water, poor quality of sealing material, lack of lubrication, overloading of condenser fan, and poor quality of cooling and circulating water. The degradation mechanisms of the condenser include erosion, corrosion, and fouling of condenser tubes, which can be caused by high-velocity water droplets, aggressive cooling water, and the accumulation of impurities, respectively. The severity of these failures can range from reduced efficiency to catastrophic failure, while their detectability can vary from visual inspection to complex testing. To prevent these failures, it is crucial to ensure the quality of components, perform regular maintenance, monitor temperature and pressure, use high-quality cooling and circulating water, and implement condition monitoring and predictive maintenance strategies.
